title: WSJ article about AI trading
author: Frodo_Baghodler
selftext: Anybody see the article yesterday about AI-designed algos and AI-advised picks? Thoughts? I see this as a huge step in stock picking moving forward. I have Schwab so I don't have access to AI stock picks but I'm wondering if I should switch to RH or something to get that functionality.

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body: I don't see why not, AI is on fire right now. Might as well try it for stocks.

replies.author: Frodo_Baghodler
replies.body: It is, but I don't really want to change brokerages if I can get 90% of the benefits just by bouncing stocks off my AI.

comments.author: TastyTrading
comments.body: I use ThetaPal AI market scouts to find nice swing trade setups

comments.author: drguid
comments.body:
I built my own model and it's pretty epic. It's just so good at finding ideal setups.

It's doing OK with real money. By the end of the year I'll know for sure.

replies.author: Frodo_Baghodler
replies.body: That's the real question. Can you share drguid?

replies.author: Frodo_Baghodler
replies.body: What kind of frequency and durations are you working with?

comments.author: peeeanuts
comments.body: I wouldn’t switch brokers just for AI picks. I’m building OpenCandle around using AI to pull the research and sources together, then making the actual investment decision myself.

replies.author: Frodo_Baghodler
replies.body: That's similar to what I'm doing now. Using AI on the outside and inputting my trades manually into Schwab.
